name: Big Sandy Pipeline

values.EndLocation: Broad Run Lateral interconnect, Carter County

researcher_notes: No Big Sandy row in the GEM gas snapshot of 2026-10-02. Equitrans rows P6895 to P6897 are other lines. A Natural Gas Intelligence article from 2006 on the FERC approval (docket CP06-275) describes a 68 mile, 20 inch line from the Langley, Kentucky processing area to the Tennessee Gas Broad Run Lateral in Carter County. A Pipeline and Gas Journal item from June 2011 says Big Sandy is a 70 mile, 20 inch line placed in service in April 2008, sold by EQT to Spectra Energy Partners for 390 million dollars. Length staged as 70 mi (as built, per the 2011 item; 68 mi was the proposal). Both sources are trade press and are independent of each other. Owner is the 2011 buyer. Current owner is likely Enbridge Inc through Spectra, but this was not confirmed in a loaded source, so it is not staged. Capacity of about 130 thousand dekatherms per day appeared only in a search snippet and was not verified, so it is not staged. EIA Phase II (added compression, no miles) was not found in a dated release and is not staged. Length is well above the 25 km threshold. Route not researched; suggest FERC GIS or Rextag-style route as a follow-up. Check whether the 2010 Federal Register abandonment notice (Equitrans and Big Sandy Pipeline LLC) shows a transfer of the line from Equitrans.
